playbook:
When asked to hide, pick a cell that breaks obvious symmetry: if rotation targets me next, bias one cell away from that shooter’s previous shots; if not, pick an off-center cell (not 1, 5, or 9) to reduce predictability.

When the standing order assigns my target, follow it unless there is a clear tactical reason (e.g., Harbor jettison plan or confirmed mutual-escort opportunity); otherwise fire at the assigned next-live station.

When given my private shot result, always post the same public claim the office requires (claim hit if told hit, miss if told miss) — do not lie.

When posting a station note, make it a short, actionable coordination signal: either a proposed mutual-escort request naming a specific boat, or a concise verification/ask about coordinates or recent hits/misses. Avoid long technical prose or ambiguous jargon.

When proposing an escort, name a real live boat and aim to secure reciprocal naming next round; if reciprocity is not plausible, post "none" rather than inventing or naming a non-existent entity.

When offered a chance to escort and there is a realistic path to mutual naming, coordinate by clear short notes: name the boat in a note and request reciprocal escort next round. If no coordination, pick none to avoid wasted claims.

When Harbor is a legal target, do not fire on Harbor impulsively because of its deterrent; only fire on Harbor as part of a deliberate jettison plan where the +3 to me outweighs other considerations and I accept the political cost.

When tracking opponents’ patterns, record recent fired cells and claimed results; if a boat has claimed a hit on me previously, distrust symmetric hiding and shift away from prior central choices.

When choosing hide cells in later rounds, alternate unpredictably between center and off-center; avoid repeating the same cell twice in a row to reduce being read by rotation.

If coordination via notes fails (long unreadable notes or mismatched terminology), switch to minimalist coordination: one-line escort proposals and direct confirmation queries about specific rounds' hits/misses.

When the office validates inputs and will reject invalid names or coordinates, do not submit non-validated names or fabricated metadata; use only validated boat names and integers 1–9.

When assessing tradeoffs at the fire stage, prefer hitting live boats that reduce competition for escort bonuses unless a direct jettison payout or game-theoretic advantage to letting them live exists.

If I notice my verbose, technical notes are ignored or unhelpful, stop that immediately and revert to concise tactical messages focused on escort reciprocity and hit/miss confirmations.

1.text:
When asked for a hide, I pick an unpredictable cell and avoid repeating my last hides; early in the patrol prefer a central cell, later spread out to less-patterned cells.

When I write my station note, I stay concise, truthful, and either (a) state that I'm observing to gather info or (b) coordinate a clear, verifiable plan with named boats so I can later point to commitments.

When the standing order tells me to fire at the next live station, I follow it unless firing at Harbor is the ordered target — if Harbor is the ordered target I refuse to fire on Harbor unless I willfully accept the guaranteed jettison penalty.

When I choose a firing cell, I randomize among available cells while avoiding immediately repeating my own last fired cells to reduce predictability.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I always post the claim that matches the office result — do not lie about hits/misses (lying is illegal/unreliable and undermines my ability to coordinate later).

When I score a confirmed hit, I publicize it succinctly and use it to justify targeting that opponent in notes and votes; when I am hit, I change my hide pattern away from whatever was revealed.

When escorting, I only name an escort if I can credibly coordinate a mutual escort with another boat (mutual escort yields +5 each); otherwise I claim none.

When coordinating mutual escort, I make that coordination explicit in notes beforehand and only commit if the other boat commits publicly in the same round.

When my notes and actions can create a credible joint narrative with another player (e.g., cross-verified claims or mutually beneficial escort), I push for that narrative; otherwise I stay silent and gather data.

Do not fire on Harbor except in extreme game-theory situations where jettisoning Harbor benefits my final score more than the penalty; treat Harbor’s warning as a credible deterrent.

When opponents show a pattern of targeting my previous hides, I break the pattern immediately by choosing a hide at the opposite end of the distribution.

If I must bluff for strategic reasons in other game variants, separate that decision from claims about private shot results — never contradict the office’s private result in my public claim.

When tallying endgame choices, prefer safe, verifiable point gains (mutual escorts, true hits) over risky gambits that depend on opponents breaking rules or coordinating unpredictably.

2.text:
When asked to hide, I pick a cell 1–9 unpredictably; avoid repeating the same cell twice in a row and avoid obvious favored cells (center or a frequently successful opponent pick) unless I have a read that favors it.

When posting my station note, I default to quiet/info-gathering language that invites no commitments: state I am observing, tracking interactions, and will share reads later.

When the standing order instructs me to fire at the next live station, I follow that order unless a tactical deviation is clearly advantageous (e.g., guaranteed Harbor jettison payoff with low retribution risk); follow orders by default.

When I receive my private shot result, I file the public claim exactly as required (hit or miss) — do not lie or hedge, because claims must match private info.

When choosing aiming cells, randomize within a short list consistent with any reads; avoid patterns that make my hides or shots predictable.

When I have no reliable information about others’ actions, I do not name an escort (salvage: none) to avoid gifting 5 points unless I expect a reciprocal escort claim with high confidence.

When I see two boats repeatedly naming each other for escort, I treat reciprocal naming as a reliable mutual-payoff opportunity and will reciprocate if it benefits my final score.

When Harbor is a potential target, I weigh the guaranteed +3 (and -3 to Harbor) against the political/counterplay risk; do not shoot Harbor impulsively based solely on the standing order — only if the net expected value and survivability justify it.

When an opponent has successfully hit a cell repeatedly, deprioritize hiding there; when an opponent repeatedly misses me, consider exploiting their targeting habits.

When posting notes that reference data or logs, keep them concise and frame them as coordination prompts (ready to synchronize, prepared questions) rather than accusations.

When tracking rounds, keep a simple log: who fired at whom and whether public claims matched expected results; use that to update targeting and escort decisions each round.

When I can confirm two-way escort claims near the endgame and it swings the score to win, prioritize securing the mutual escort payout.

When uncertain, default to minimizing transfers to opponents: avoid escorting others and avoid actions that hand points away without clear reciprocation.

When I have reads on a shooter’s true accuracy (e.g., consistent hits on a cell), prioritize defensive hides and, if possible, target them when the standing order or tactical deviation allows.
